sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Ascom is a small, non-deposit-taking lender whose investment case depends on collectable credit and the economics of capital deployment, not its small market capitalization. Reported equity of ₹55.0043 crore and CAR of 102.88% support accounting resilience, but five-year revenue growth of about 4.07%, reported ROE near 9.98%, connected lending of 42.48% of the loan book and an observed roughly 4× book quote do not establish a compounder. This is a conditional value/credit-underwriting review on hold, not a misconduct conclusion. The decisive missing evidence is borrower-level realization and loss history. [S1, S3, H1, M1]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Ascom Leasing & Investments Limited, ASCOM, INE08KD01015, NSE SME. Cutoff October 20, 2026; the last available observed trade is October 16 at ₹187.45, not an executable October 20 quote. Current issued shares are 11,714,179; market capitalization is ₹219.5821 crore. Standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards are the appropriate scope; no subsidiary perimeter was disclosed. Five-year investor horizon runs October 20, 2026 to October 20, 2031, with a 15% nominal pretax hurdle and an illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity reference, not a recommended position. G1/G3/G4 are conditional; G2 is an evidence hold on lender asset/income realization. Historical aggregate inputs are High confidence; governance and capital-return judgment Medium; collection-normalized investment conclusions Low. Forecast uncertainty is distinct from correctly retrieving the audited numbers. [S1, S3, M1]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS, GQS and IAS are NS. The quality factors are GOV 4, MOAT 3, REV 2, DUR 4, CAP 4, CASH NS, BAL 6, EXEC 5 and EARN 5. IAS has R NS, D 2, P 1 and L 1; quality is reused only through BQS. BQS and GQS each have 90% evidence coverage, with missing-factor bounds 3.50–4.40 and 3.05–3.95 respectively. IAS known-factor coverage is 40%, with a mathematical bound 1.20–6.60. These are missing-data bounds, not estimated scores or confidence intervals. No weights are redistributed and no adverse cap substitutes for NS. Changing GOV and CAP by one point each moves BQS by up to 0.32; moving CAP and EARN moves GQS by up to 0.30, without curing missing CASH. The evidence audit provides positive and contrary facts for each scoreable factor. [S1, S3, H1–H4, M1]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company makes secured mortgage/property loans and unsecured personal loans, with the latter described as lending to salaried, government and semi-government employees supported by personal guarantees. FY26 noncurrent financing receivables were ₹43.9165 crore and current financing receivables ₹2.0704 crore. Secured property balances totaled ₹42.5198 crore and personal-guarantee balances ₹3.4671 crore; these are loan principal, not revenue. Financing interest was ₹12.7945 crore and bank-deposit interest ₹0.2687 crore, with rounding to reported total income ₹13.0633 crore. Loan income is accrued over contract periods; income on classified problem assets and overdue charges is recognized on receipt according to the policy. A separate ₹3.8821 crore trade balance is disclosed without a sufficiently detailed composition bridge to identify it all as interest. Management cites property LTV near 50%, or 60–65% for renovation loans; those are management valuations, not independently established liquidation cover for Marvella. [S1 pp.87–91]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The proposed advantage is local borrower knowledge and flexible service: these may improve origination and collection, but the mechanism needs sustained loss-adjusted cohort evidence. A high nominal loan yield is compensation for servicing, credit and concentration risk, not proof of pricing power. The nearly flat loan book, falling yield/NIM and material connected exposure do not demonstrate a scalable underwriting or low-cost funding advantage. Bajaj Finance is a diversified underwriting/distribution comparator, Cholamandalam a vehicle/LAP underwriting comparator, and Five-Star Business Finance a secured small-business lending comparator; their scale, borrower mix, provisioning framework and funding differ materially. No peer price multiple is imported and no numerical same-risk peer ranking is claimed. Ascom’s own FY24 discussion acknowledges low entry barriers and competition from banks, NBFCs and fintechs. Public, issuer-specific collection data is the decisive comparison still missing. [S1, H4]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Recognized revenue in FY21–FY26 was ₹10.6960, ₹12.4463, ₹12.1511, ₹12.3344, ₹12.9216 and ₹13.0633 crore. The five-year CAGR is 4.07%; the three-year FY23–FY26 CAGR is 2.44%. Annual additions were approximately ₹1.7503, −₹0.2952, ₹0.1833, ₹0.5873 and ₹0.1417 crore. FY26 growth was 1.10%, while the loan portfolio rose 1.71%. Financing interest rose only about 0.57%; bank-deposit interest contributed ₹0.0695 crore of the roughly ₹0.1417 crore income addition. Loan yield declined from 29.72% to 28.06% and NIM from 27.11% to 25.67%. The preferred five-year window is comparable, includes the pandemic period without selecting its trough, and is not replaced by an exciting early small-base ten-year percentage. Organic/acquired decomposition has no known subsidiary acquisition, but borrower volume, repricing and mix are not separately disclosed. No post-March 2026 interim financial result was verified. [H1–H4, S4, S1]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: A lender expands by collecting existing assets, retaining earnings and funding new principal, not by declaring a large addressable market. Reported FY26 ROE is 9.98% versus an analyst equity-cost range of 14–18%. The five-year change in PAT divided by added equity is only about 1.74%, a capital-productivity diagnostic rather than a cohort IRR. Capital is plentiful in accounting terms, but its sustainable return is unproven. The model’s base/bull loan-growth ambitions are 4%/10%, with explicit yield, credit loss, income collection, expense inflation and capital assumptions. Originations are constrained to available internal cash; no new funding or exercise of the ₹100 crore related-party authority is assumed. A 25% expansion path without financing runs short of cash, so it has no shareholder IRR. The authority is an approved five-year maximum, not an outstanding loan, committed funding line or growth forecast. GQS remains NS because the realization evidence needed for a lender-specific CASH score is incomplete. [S1, S3; analyst model]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Tushar Rohitbhai Pandya is managing director and CFO; family remuneration and lending concentration are material economic issues. FY26 director remuneration was ₹2.5656 crore, 49.08% of PAT, unchanged from FY25. Related loans increased to ₹19.5374 crore, including ₹19.3426 crore to Marvella Realty. Marvella received ₹6.45 crore new advances, repaid ₹4.01 crore and generated ₹2.6972 crore reported interest; these disclosed repayments are important contrary evidence to treating the whole balance as non-performing. The September 30 AGM approved a ₹100 crore aggregate five-year related-party ceiling, with ₹25 crore for each named counterparty. Resolution 4 passed on 56,500 public votes; 7,805,914 interested promoter votes were excluded. Approval does not validate recoverability. The statutory audit was unmodified and CARO reported no lender default. Separately, the secretarial auditor observed that two independent directors had not qualified the IICA online proficiency test; management acknowledged the observation and said it advised completion of applicable requirements. Later completion was not verified. This is a dated compliance disclosure, not an independently adjudicated current violation. The May company-secretary resignation and August appointment were disclosed; the September AGM was completed. [S1 pp.21–23,41–42,56,67–78,89,93; S3; U3, U11, U17]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: The seven-year table preserves reported lender CFO, but does not score industrial CFO/PAT. FY24/FY25/FY26 CFO was −₹0.1625/₹0.5444/₹4.8258 crore; financing principal and current debt movements are embedded, and interest paid is in financing cash flow. FY26 CFO of ₹4.8258 less cash capex ₹0.6808 plus financing flow −₹5.5140 equals the ₹1.3690 crore fall in reported cash, within ₹0.0001 crore displayed rounding. Cash of ₹4.9239 includes ₹3.1851 crore FDs, against which SBI debt of ₹1.5996 is secured. Only ₹1.7388 is treated as initially free. Opening tax ₹1.7385 and credit ₹1.2517, TDS ₹0.2987, other payables ₹0.1735, debt ₹2.3595 and standard provision ₹0.115 are each assigned one treatment. Capital advance ₹2.6 has persisted since FY24; it is not free cash or ordinary WC. Trade receivables above six months increased from ₹2.7800 to ₹3.2678 crore despite total trade receivables falling to ₹3.8821; ₹1.1312 is aged 2–3 years. These are separate trade ageing figures, not loan GNPA. The ₹0.0019 crore annual provision charge is a standard-asset reserve movement, not proof of negligible realized losses. Detailed rounded opening assets and liabilities both total ₹59.6895 versus printed ₹59.6894; this is a ₹1,000 presentation difference, not missing cash. The complete claim register and cash/loan/equity identities reconcile. [S1 pp.79–98, S4, H1–H3]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹187.45, observed P/E is 42.01× and P/B 3.99×. The lender model begins with March 31 actual stocks and forecasts the unobserved bridge to October entry; it does not present that bridge as reported results. All 68 dated intervals separately model loan principal, loan interest, trade recovery, new income accruals, provisions, cash expenses, tax, capex, debt, capital and distributions. Base/bear/bull terminal P/B assumptions are 0.8/0.5/1.2, applied to net common equity without adding cash or subtracting debt twice. Conditional terminal prices are ₹54.29/₹21.64/₹93.53; diagnostic XIRRs are -21.57%/-35.07%/-12.28%. These are analyst scenarios, not endorsed fair values or a scoreable R. Base hurdle-entry sensitivities are ₹32.49, ₹28.57 and ₹25.22 at 12%,15%,18% hurdles, before transaction costs. The two-way growth/PB grid and residual-income cross-check are explicit. At base terminal book, today’s price needs about 5.51× exit P/B to earn 15%, or about 58% annual book-per-share growth at 0.8× exit. Such hurdles are not supported by historical growth or ROE. The September dividend belongs to September 18 record-date holders and is not added to an October 20 buyer’s return. [S1,S3,M1; analyst model]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest adverse case is connected-principal loss plus weaker realized interest, slower loan collections, fixed expenses and multiple normalization. The ordinary bear writes off 25% of Marvella exposure and 50% of the separate trade and capital-advance balances, then applies recurring 2.5% loan credit cost. It remains funded without rescue in the model but ends at ₹21.64, a 88.5% price loss. A 50% Marvella loss, complete legacy trade/capital-advance impairment and 50% interest collection exhaust cash: maximum negative cash is ₹3.9612 crore. No investor IRR is shown for that unfunded path. A separate immediate 50% expense-reset path self-funds with minimum cash ₹0.9008, but this uncommitted response is not assumed in the ordinary severe case. Loss accounting is noncash; it reduces recoverable loan stock once, while actual collections and any replacement lending drive cash. The thesis-break variable is collectable loan/income value, not a quoted drawdown. Permanent impairment risk at this valuation is High. No present default, fraud or forced liquidation is asserted. [S1,S3; analyst stress model]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five-year 5×/10× price gain needs 38.0%/58.5% annual per-share growth if the multiple does not change. At the FY26 reported ROE near 10%, full retention alone compounds book only about 1.61× over five years, before losses; actual dividends modestly reduce retained growth. A normalization from about 4× to 1× book can overwhelm such accumulation. Keeping shares constant is favorable; any future equity raise must add cash and dilution together. The model provides no evidence-backed 5×/10× path, so the outcome is Speculative / unsupported, not a small-cap optionality bonus. [S1,H1,M1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: 1. Loan arrears, GNPA/NNPA, restructurings and cohort losses: presently not adequately established; require reconciliation to principal and provisions before lifting CASH/R hold. 2. Separate trade ageing: baseline ₹3.2678 crore beyond six months and ₹1.1312 aged 2–3 years; investigate any further ageing or unsupported classification as good. 3. Connected lending: baseline ₹19.5374 crore/42.48%, with Marvella ₹19.3426; require borrower-specific cash receipts and collateral before treating more authority as growth. 4. Capital and liquidity: reported CAR 102.88%, FDs ₹3.1851 and debt ₹2.3595; verify release restrictions, debt installments and all tax/statutory settlements. 5. Economic returns: ROE of 9.98%, revenue growth 1.10%; investigate persistent equity accumulation without loss-adjusted ROE improvement. 6. Capital advance ₹2.6: seek delivery, refund, counterparty and impairment evidence, not another unverified completion promise. 7. Remuneration/compliance: director pay ₹2.5656, new family employment approvals and the secretarial observation; verify actual payments and corrective compliance. 8. Trading: 7/60 observed sessions, 500-share lot; require live depth and sustained trading before implementation. These are research review triggers, not automatic sell rules or an active monitoring service. [S1,S3,M1]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved lender evidence. BQS/GQS/IAS are incomplete and excluded from numerical rankings, not placed last as if scored poorly. The record does not meet compounder criteria and supplies no portfolio allocation or trade instruction. Research priority is conditional: borrower collections, loss recognition and connected-credit economics matter more than another headline growth approval. A lower price alone cannot cure the missing realization evidence, although it would reduce the required economic hurdle. A verified asset-quality reconciliation, sustained collection and better risk-adjusted returns could change the assessment; no wrongdoing is presumed from disclosure gaps. [S1,S3; model and factor audits]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary financial history was recovered through FY21/FY22/FY23 annuals, FY24 narrative and FY25/FY26 signed statements; scanned decisive balances were visually checked. Exact dated source URLs and locators are in the ledger. Official market observations through October 19 establish the last observed October 16 quote, lot and trading frequency; they are not live depth. New public events reviewed include September AGM/dividend decisions, October share-capital filing cover, company-secretary changes and April encumbrance disclosure. No later actual interim balance was verified. Open questions are loan vintages and arrears, interest versus trade-stock composition, recoveries and collateral by related borrower, deployment of approved authority, capital-advance completion, and completion of the secretarial action. The cash/capital scenarios deliberately expose these uncertainties; they do not overwrite issuer accounts. Severe-case cost cuts, collection rates, loss percentages, terminal P/B and credit-release timing are analyst assumptions. Financial models and methodology scores are judgment tools, not validated predictors. [S1,S3,S4,H1–H4,U0,U3,U11,U17,U22,M1]

GOV.reason: Related credit of 42.48% and pay of 49.08% of PAT constrain stewardship assessment; contrary: interested voting excluded, statutory audit unmodified and no verified abuse.

MOAT.reason: Small local loan book, contestable lending and limited demonstrated underwriting edge; contrary: long operating record, profitable secured/personal lending. High yield alone is not a moat.

REV.reason: Five-year recognized revenue CAGR of 4.07%, FY26 growth of 1.10%; no trajectory adjustment. Contrary: positive growth and no acquisition-perimeter distortion.

DUR.reason: Household/property credit offers demand, and high capital permits deployment; concentrated connected lending and no evidenced loss-adjusted scalable channel restrict accessible runway.

CAP.reason: Reported ROE of 9.98% is below the 14–18% assumed equity cost, and incremental PAT/book added is about 1.74%; contrary: positive earnings and large accounting capital. Cohort return remains unknown.

CASH.reason: Loan vintages, principal arrears and accrual realization remain unverified. Aged separate trade balances demand investigation but are not loan NPA; auditor says repayments generally received. Neither industrial CFO/PAT nor missing GNPA yields a default numeric score.

BAL.reason: Reported CAR 102.88%, debt reduction and ordinary-bear self-funding support resilience; concentrated assets, restricted FDs and severe income/collection stress prevent a stronger claim.

EXEC.reason: Positive six-year profits and debt repayment demonstrate continuity; contrary: slow revenue growth and limited verified diversification. AGM approval is completed governance procedure, not deployment performance.

EARN.reason: Recurring lending revenue and bonus-adjusted EPS of 4.09→4.46 since FY21 are positive; declining ROE/NIM and unverified credit normalization temper quality. Separate loan-loss and CASH uncertainty retained.

R.reason: Funded diagnostic cases exist but missing validated collection/loss inputs prevent a supported base-case return score.

D.reason: Approximately 4× book entry exposes investors to large loss even without insolvency. Bear terminal price of 21.64 implies 88.46% price loss; severe collections can cause cash shortage. High reported capital is contrary support.

P.reason: Base capital path needs about 5.51× exit book for a 15% hurdle, or about 58% annual book-per-share growth at 0.8× exit; unsupported against 4.07% revenue and about 10% reported ROE. Positive earnings are acknowledged.

L.reason: 7/60 observed sessions, zero conditional median and a 500-share lot give no finite conservative exit capacity; contrary: verified SM eligibility and actual October trades. No suspension claim.

assumptions_note: All April–October 2026 bridge cash flows are forecasts, not observed interim results.
All fixed deposits are conservatively blocked until SBI debt is retired in the first model interval; release is a financing assumption.
Only year-one principal amount has a disclosed current-balance anchor; thereafter 20% annual runoff and collection efficiency are explicit sensitivities, not verified ALM.
No deposits, new borrowing, shareholder capital, dilution, committed facilities or use of approved related-party ceiling is assumed.
Operating cash flow/PAT, EV/EBITDA and industrial ROIC are not scoring metrics for this lender.
Capital ratio is an analytical equity/risk-asset proxy with 20% minimum stress reference, not a reconstructed regulatory compliance ratio.
Tax losses receive no immediate tax refund; existing credits are used or recovered once, separately from WC.
Existing standard reserve is used once against modeled loan loss and replenished to 0.25%; loss recognition itself is noncash and only actual collections/disbursements affect cash.
Trade ageing is not loan NPA. No identification of the legacy trade stock as accrued interest is asserted.
Post-entry distributions require positive earnings and cash after obligations; 20% statutory transfer is within equity. Declared September dividend belongs to pre-entry record-date holders.
Terminal P/B applies to net common equity including cash and all residual claims. No excess-cash double count.
Severe cost-reset alternative cuts the entire expense base 50% from the first forecast interval; this is a conditional uncommitted management response, not a fact or baseline survival claim.
New loan originations begin yielding from the next interval; this conservative timing avoids intra-month interest circularity.
No scenario probability, forecast recommendation or current-default allegation.

reverse_expectations.note: CAGR is a hurdle proxy using March 2026 reported book over the five-year investor horizon, not an exact October-entry book CAGR or a forecast; the funded reverse path requires profitable loan deployment and validated losses.

valuation.method: Conditional lender equity cash flow and terminal net-book sensitivity, with residual-income cross-check. No endorsed fair value or supported R score.
valuation.forecast_uncertainty: Very high: publicly verified borrower vintages, loss experience and subsequent lending deployments are inadequate for underwriting the model.
